chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the one who remarries but did not have witnesses testify, he said: 'Having witnesses testify is more beloved to me, but I do not see harm in what he did.'
ai.seo_question: Is a remarriage valid if no witnesses were present for the new contract?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the status of the *Khula* or remarriage contract when witnesses are omitted, distinguishing between the ideal practice (*mustahabb*) and legal validity (*sahih*). This reflects the Shia juristic principle that while witnessing is a recommended pillar to ensure public recognition and prevent disputes, its absence does not invalidate the marriage contract itself. The ruling underscores the flexibility in personal status laws, prioritizing the validity of the union over strict procedural formalities unless specified otherwise.
